svg.title: Terminal output and reusable storage are different events
svg.desc: Record request identity, allocation generation, event clock and observation scope
svg.text: Terminal output and reusable storage are different events
Record request identity, allocation generation, event clock and observation scope
Scheduled arrival → actual ingress → authorized work
Preserve dispatch lag and queue waiting; independent demand must not vanish in stalls.
Report caller latency separately from intended-demand latency and allocator operation time.
Final output or cancellation → detach owner edge
An existing reader or writer may still hold a lifetime pin.
A timeout or callback submission does not prove completion or authorize slot reuse.
Known access completion → safe return → optional backing release
Retained cache ownership can legitimately keep a prefix alive.
Unknown completion stays protected; pool-free capacity may remain allocated outside.
Minimal timing → focused profile → minimal validation again
Correlate host ranges and device dependencies; include observer memory and overhead.
Constructed path: 1 + 2 + 7 + 1 = 11 ms; halved allocation gives 10 ms, not 5.5 ms.
Count all offered outcomes. Keep successful latency, cancellation and resource recovery populations separate.
